title: One authority. Two shores.
coordinate_note: Approximate portal, plaza or terminal areas read from public maps. Lines are straight schematic links between the two shores, not surveyed tunnel or track alignments.

crossings.name: PATH uptown tubes
crossings.pa_role: Opened by the Hudson & Manhattan Railroad; taken over by the Port Authority in 1962 and renamed PATH.

crossings.name: PATH downtown tubes
crossings.pa_role: Opened by the Hudson & Manhattan Railroad; taken over by the Port Authority in 1962.

crossings.name: Holland Tunnel
crossings.pa_role: Built by the bi-state tunnel commissions; placed under Port Authority control in 1930.

crossings.name: George Washington Bridge
crossings.pa_role: Built by the Port Authority; completed October 1931.

crossings.name: Lincoln Tunnel
crossings.pa_role: Built by the Port Authority: first tube 1937, second 1945, third 1957.

landmarks.name: World Trade Center
landmarks.note: Port Authority campus; original towers dedicated April 4, 1973.

landmarks.name: Port Authority Bus Terminal
landmarks.note: Port Authority bus terminal in Midtown, fed by the Lincoln Tunnel.

landmarks.name: GWB Bus Station
landmarks.note: Port Authority bus station at the bridge's Manhattan end.

pair_links.01: Port Authority link: Lower Manhattan’s skyline is anchored by the World Trade Center, a Port Authority site. PATH trains run under the river between these two shores.
pair_links.02: Port Authority link: the Lincoln Tunnel runs under this stretch of river, from Weehawken to Midtown and the Port Authority Bus Terminal.
pair_links.03: Port Authority link: the George Washington Bridge was built by the Port Authority and opened in 1931. The lighthouse sits at the foot of its New York tower.
